decisions.title: Semantic authority precedence
decisions.decision: Normative schemas, ADRs, mathematical contracts, and language-neutral fixtures outrank any individual implementation or research recommendation.
decisions.reason: Prevents TypeScript, Swift, or a generated mockup from becoming an accidental specification.

decisions.title: Project schema v2 and exact wire arithmetic
decisions.decision: Use canonical decimal strings for arbitrary-size rational numerator/denominator values; preserve source bytes/digest separately from normalized semantic model/digest.
decisions.reason: Exact musical time and future migration cannot rely on JSON numbers or destructive canonicalization.

decisions.title: Logical package and physical container profiles
decisions.decision: Define one logical AGL package and permit native-directory and portable-archive physical profiles with the same logical member set and semantic package hash.
decisions.reason: A directory package is natural on iPad, while browser interchange generally requires an archive; the logical format must remain one product contract.

decisions.title: Project state versus studio session state
decisions.decision: Persist authored semantic/project state and selected presentation metadata only; keep selection, focus, hover, transport, audio route, workspace layout, preview, and runtime state outside the semantic project digest.
decisions.reason: Avoids nondeterministic files, noisy undo history, and platform-specific project semantics.

decisions.title: Conformance-first selective core
decisions.decision: Keep TypeScript as the browser reference during stabilization, implement only required Swift semantics, and share schemas/fixtures before sharing implementation.
decisions.reason: This is the least-regret path while the project schema and evaluator semantics are still changing.

decisions.title: Shared systems core evidence gate
decisions.decision: Do not adopt Rust, Swift/Wasm, or production JavaScriptCore now; JSC is a pinned test oracle only, and a shared kernel requires measured workload or maintenance evidence.
decisions.reason: No evidence-grade AGL benchmark currently establishes the burden of proof for a third production toolchain.

decisions.title: Three temporal domains
decisions.decision: Keep exact rational musical/source time above audio, resolve analytic/tempo mappings into ideal seconds in the backend-neutral audio plan, then quantize once into integer sample frames.
decisions.reason: Risset event seconds are generally logarithmic and not rational, while project beat semantics must remain exact.

decisions.title: Canonical audio plan boundary
decisions.decision: One immutable, backend-neutral ResolvedAudioPlan drives real-time and offline rendering; native and web schedules are derived projections, not alternate event models.
decisions.reason: Creates a meaningful equivalence boundary without promising cross-engine PCM identity.

decisions.title: Sample-frame quantization v1
decisions.decision: For nonnegative ideal seconds, sample frame v1 is floor(seconds * sampleRate + 0.5); the conversion version is recorded in plan/provenance.
decisions.reason: A versioned absolute-time mapping prevents accumulated rounding drift; boundary fixtures remain mandatory.

decisions.title: Browser audio responsibility split
decisions.decision: Dedicated Worker evaluates graphs and expands plans; the main thread owns AudioContext/control-plane scheduling; AudioWorklet owns bounded DSP and dense event dispatch only.
decisions.reason: Matches platform exposure and keeps unbounded domain work off the rendering thread.

decisions.title: Adaptive look-ahead scheduler
decisions.decision: Benchmark from a 25 ms wake, 100 ms horizon, adaptive growth from observed jitter, and a provisional 250 ms ceiling; treat all numeric thresholds as calibration candidates.
decisions.reason: The architecture is accepted, but cross-browser/device measurements remain a release gate.

decisions.title: Generation-based audio cutover
decisions.decision: Edits, seeks, loops, and plan revisions create generation IDs and future cutover times/frames; stale native/worklet events are silenced or rejected, while already-emitted audio is history.
decisions.reason: Provides one backend-independent cancellation and live-edit semantic.

decisions.title: Canonical sonification pipeline
decisions.decision: Use explicit versioned stages: Source → Sample → Normalize → Smooth → Transform → Quantize/Threshold → Constrain → Target, allowing repeated stages but no hidden shaping.
decisions.reason: Sampling, normalization, smoothing, and musicality are authored representational choices, not renderer details.

decisions.title: Temporal semantics of mappings
decisions.decision: Every mapping declares pointwise, causal-stateful, bounded-lookahead, or whole-window/frozen semantics; live zero-latency graphs reject future-dependent stages.
decisions.reason: Prevents acausal normalization or smoothing from silently changing previously produced live output.

decisions.title: Explicit randomness and constraints
decisions.decision: Random variation is a seeded/keyed operator; musical constraints are deterministic downstream stages with hard/soft priority and traceable deltas.
decisions.reason: Supports reproducibility and explains how final musical output differs from raw mapped data.

decisions.title: One studio, three workspace projections
decisions.decision: Explore, Compose, and Inspect are layout/emphasis presets over one project, selection, command bus, transport, and undo history; they are not capability modes.
decisions.reason: Reduces density without creating multiple semantic products or hidden permission boundaries.

decisions.title: Selection, focus, hover, and relations are distinct
decisions.decision: Maintain actionable selection, primary selection, keyboard focus, pointer hover, related/provenance highlight, range anchors, and orphaned generated references separately.
decisions.reason: Focus navigation must remain cheap and must not silently change command intent or trigger expensive selection work.

decisions.title: Semantic gesture lifecycle
decisions.decision: High-frequency interaction uses begin → preview* → commit/cancel; preview never mutates canonical project/history, and one continuous gesture creates at most one transaction.
decisions.reason: Pointer sample rate is not semantic history granularity.

decisions.title: Authoritative command envelope and inverses
decisions.decision: Commands carry project epoch, transaction/action identity, actor/origin metadata, schema versions, canonical target/write sets, and fine-grained preconditions; the core derives inverses from validated pre-state.
decisions.reason: Global revision equality alone is too coarse, and UI-supplied inverses are unsafe.

decisions.title: Generated identity capability
decisions.decision: Every generator declares stable, successor-mapped, or ephemeral output identity. Missing generated references never retarget by proximity.
decisions.reason: Sparse exceptions and persistent generated selection are only valid when correspondence semantics are explicit.

decisions.title: Material model uses separate axes
decisions.decision: Persist material kind (user-authored/live-generated/snapshot/edited-derivative) and source linkage; compute source status (current/changed/missing/detached) from the semantic dependency digest rather than storing a flat state enum.
decisions.reason: Staleness is a source relationship, not a material origin, and unrelated project edits must not stale a snapshot.

decisions.title: Prepare-then-commit materialization
decisions.decision: Materialization evaluates a half-open exact interval asynchronously, records immutable lineage and content-addressed artifacts, and commits only if the relevant source dependency digest still matches.
decisions.reason: Prevents freezing a result different from the one the user requested.

decisions.title: Temporary A/B overrides deferred
decisions.decision: Do not include A/B overrides in MVP canonical architecture until edit routing, baseline drift, local/global undo, nesting, and commit/rebase semantics are resolved.
decisions.reason: The research identifies unresolved architecture-level behavior rather than a safe implementation contract.

decisions.title: Classical Risset terminology
decisions.decision: Define rhythm.risset@1 with 2:1 tempo-octave equivalence; expose other ratios as generalized barberpole-tempo behavior.
decisions.reason: Preserves historical/mathematical terminology while retaining the generalized kernel.

decisions.title: Risset envelope and default reconciliation
decisions.decision: Make envelope domain and normalization explicit. Use the completed DR-01 report default: raised-cosine linear partition, half-width B=2, 20 s cycle, 120 BPM reference; retain nominal equal-power/L2 as a comparison mode, and label all perceptual defaults provisional.
decisions.reason: The report supplies a cleaner B=2 constant-sum derivation; the packet proposed a conflicting power-domain default without access to the report body.

decisions.title: Orthogonal Risset stages
decisions.decision: Core Risset owns rate law, analytic phase, envelope, normalization, and direction; subdivision shedding, metric ambiguity, anchor pulse, and pitch coupling are separate bypassable stages.
decisions.reason: Supports controlled experiments, provenance, undo, and honest user-facing claims.

decisions.title: Exact Penrose production construction
decisions.decision: Use a certified regular de Bruijn pentagrid emitting P3 rhombs, exact integer/Q(phi) topology, stable line/tuple IDs, and cut-and-project/Robinson validation oracles.
decisions.reason: The mathematical choice is accepted, but fixture bytes, legal-star corpus, matching decoration corpus, and prototype receipts must be checked in before completion.

decisions.title: Penrose query and clipping semantics
decisions.decision: A finite patch is a query into one configured infinite tiling; clipping is visualization-only, synthetic clip edges never create adjacency, and completeness/halo status is explicit.
decisions.reason: Prevents viewport state from changing mathematical identity or inventing topology.

decisions.title: Native client as ports-and-adapters
decisions.decision: Native iPad uses canonical schemas/commands/plans/projections with SwiftUI, AVAudioEngine, Core MIDI, Metal, and Files as adapters; one active audible project per process is the MVP policy.
decisions.reason: Process-global audio/session resources and limited staffing make a second product core or multi-project mixer premature.

decisions.title: MIDI posture
decisions.decision: Web MIDI is optional progressive enhancement; native uses UMP/MIDIEventList internally and down-converts only at explicit MIDI 1 or Standard MIDI File boundaries.
decisions.reason: Avoids making nonportable browser capability or 7-bit fields canonical.

decisions.title: Accessibility from shared semantics
decisions.decision: Every auditory, visual, motion, graph, and geometry meaning must have an equivalent semantic/text/keyboard representation generated from the same model; no core operation is drag-only or color-only.
decisions.reason: Accessibility cannot be reconstructed reliably from pixels or audio after implementation.

decisions.title: Scientific claim registry
decisions.decision: User-facing claims carry evidence status: direct, qualified, experimental, or prohibited; presets also record evidence provenance and product-defined validation thresholds.
decisions.reason: Separates theorem/evidence from engineering defaults and avoids presenting finite visualizations or unvalidated presets as scientific proof.

decisions.title: Semantic and execution provenance split
decisions.decision: Semantic provenance records source/operator/version/seed/profile/lineage; execution provenance separately records backend/build/browser/device/sample rate/approximations and performance.
decisions.reason: Backend identity must not contaminate project meaning, while reproducibility still requires execution receipts.

decisions.title: Async acceptance barrier
decisions.decision: Derived results become current only when project epoch, scope, channel, generation, input digest, semantic-environment digest, and integrity all match; cancellation is resource control, not freshness proof.
decisions.reason: Prevents out-of-order results from overwriting current preview or committed state.

decisions.title: Performance limits remain empirical
decisions.decision: Treat scheduler, event-density, geometry, memory, shared-core, and device thresholds as provisional benchmark profiles until accepted workloads run on declared environments.
decisions.reason: The reports provide architectures and harnesses, not physical browser/iPad measurements.

decisions.title: Realtime callback isolation
decisions.decision: No project decoding, graph evaluation, BigInt/exact geometry, provenance allocation, JavaScript VM, locks, file/network I/O, or unbounded work may execute in an audio render callback.
decisions.reason: This is a hard platform invariant independent of implementation language.
